title: One Rational Number, and a Stress-Test of the Inverted-Black-Hole Null
description: An addendum to 'The Inverted Black Hole' (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20947913) and 'One Free Number' (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20938891). Three results, one of them a correction of presentation in the parent papers. FIRST, THE COEFFICIENT REDUCES TO A SINGLE RATIONAL. The parent note writes a0 = cH_Lambda/Z with Z = sqrt(32pi/3), factored as the Einstein coupling 8pi times the Friedmann 3 with a single free outside factor of 2. That factorisation is now exact and complete: writing 32pi as 8pi/kappa^2 and substituting Lambda = 8 pi G rho_Lambda / c^2, EVERY pi, the 32 and the 3 ALL CANCEL, leaving a0 = kappa * c * sqrt(G rho_Lambda) exactly, with kappa = 1/2 (verified symbolically). So '32pi/3' is not a compound of three geometric factors -- it is an artifact of routing one statement through Lambda and Einstein's 8pi. The framework's entire dimensionless content is the single RATIONAL kappa = 1/2, and the honest form of the open problem is 'why kappa = 1/2', not 'why 32pi/3'. This strengthens the One Free Number thesis: the number is not merely single, it is rational. It also relocates the standing transcendence obstruction -- 'Z carries a transcendental sqrt(pi) while flavour data is algebraic' is correct about Z, but Z's sqrt(pi) comes from EINSTEIN's 8pi, i.e. from general relativity, NOT from this framework, whose own number is rational. SECOND, THE INVERTED-BLACK-HOLE NULL SURVIVES A DELIBERATE ATTACK, for a stronger reason than the parent note gave. That note argues the universal crossover r_cross = sqrt(Z) r_s = 2.406 r_s -- mass-independent, and sitting between the photon sphere at 1.5 r_s and the ISCO at 3 r_s, i.e. inside the ngEHT/LISA band -- self-cancels into exact GR via (a) mass-independence and (b) the free-fall / Hartle-Hawking theorem. Argument (b) protects only GEODESIC observers, which is a real gap: a STATIC observer at radius r has proper acceleration (GM/r^2)/sqrt(1 - r_s/r), which is non-zero and diverges at the horizon. Evaluating the framework's own interpolation nu(y) = sqrt(1+1/y) for exactly that observer at exactly r_cross, with the framework's operative COSMIC a0, gives fractional deviations from Newtonian inertia of 1.36e-22 (stellar 10 Msun), 5.85e-17 (Sgr A*) and 8.85e-14 (M87*), against a pre-declared interest threshold of 1e-6: the worst case is 1.1e7 times below anything ngEHT or LISA could notice. A tidal channel fares worse -- the kernel takes Box_u u rather than |a|, and being maximally generous (body size L = r) gives a_tid ~ c^2 r_s/r^2, which at r_cross sits 5.6e21, 1.3e16 and 8.6e12 times a0 for the three holes, i.e. MORE deeply switched off. And solving a_proper(r) = a0 returns the a0 shell at r = sqrt(GM/a0): 0.122 pc, 80 pc and 3.1 kpc, which are 1.3e11, 1.9e8 and 5.0e6 Schwarzschild radii. The framework meets a black hole parsecs to kiloparsecs outside it, never at the horizon; r_cross = 2.406 r_s is where the FORMAL DUAL would switch on, not where the framework's physics does. So r_cross remains a prediction of EXACTLY-GR shadows, ISCO frequencies, ringdown spectra and inspiral waveforms. Both a0 footings carried throughout (canonical cH_Lambda/Z = 9.36e-11, alternate cH0/Z = 1.13e-10). THIRD, AND STATED AGAINST INTEREST, THE PARENT NOTE CARRIES A PRESENTATIONAL RISK A REFEREE WILL FIND. It explicitly rejects the objection 'g >> a0 near a horizon, so the effect vanishes', on the correct ground that the formal dual a0_BH = c^4/(4 G M Z) scales up identically and keeps a/a0_BH of order unity down to the horizon -- indeed we find nu - 1 = 0.3283 at r_cross, IDENTICAL for all three holes, a clean exhibition of the mass-independence. But the framework's OPERATIVE scale is the cosmic a0, by its own section 1.2 (inertia responds to the bath of the inverted cosmic horizon), and at that scale the effect DOES vanish, by about 22 orders. Both statements are true of different scales, and at fixed radius the two readings differ by 3.7e12. The rejection is sound as written but reads as a claim of a real strong-field signal, and this addendum supplies the one sentence that fixes it. TWO KEPT NUMBERS FROM THE DE SITTER SIDE. T_dS/T_U(a0) = Z exactly (canonical footing), the coefficient restated as a pure temperature ratio; and the a0 shell of the maximal (Nariai) de Sitter black hole coincides with the de Sitter horizon, sqrt(Z/(3 sqrt 3)) = 1.0555 canonical and 0.9616 alternate, within 6% of unity from pure numbers with no fit -- reported WITH its ~2%-by-chance prior, so a structural coincidence and NOT a derivation of Z. Making it more would require deriving Z from the Schwarzschild-de Sitter double-root constant 3 sqrt 3, which is the kappa-forcing route, closed 2026-06-17 by ghost-freedom, unitarity and holography. Unchanged and NOT a framework result: every black hole de Sitter permits does evaporate, because the equilibrium mass 1.299 x M_Nariai is forbidden so T_+ > T_c across 40 decades of mass -- that is Gibbons & Hawking (1977) in plain GR + Lambda. Modified inertia contributes NOTHING to it: at a stellar horizon y = g/a0 ~ 1e23 and nu - 1 = 3.1e-23. Black holes are the most purely general-relativistic objects this framework knows, which is precisely why it survives the solar system. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. No new observable. No derivation of Z, kappa, the response sign, or a0's value -- all remain POSTULATED. The strong-field axis stays a NULL whose discriminating power is against metric-shifting completions such as MOG, and NOT against this framework or against AeST, whose published black holes are stealth (Skordis & Zlosnik, arXiv:2412.15395). Credit as in the parent papers: the interpolation nu(y) = sqrt(1+1/y) and the identity g_obs^2 - g_bar^2 = a0 g_bar ARE Milgrom (1999, Phys. Lett. A 253, 273) Eqs. (8)-(9); the a0-Lambda tie is Milgrom's and Smolin's with a 2pi coefficient and NO PRIORITY IS CLAIMED for it. What is ours is the coefficient cH_Lambda/Z, the modified-inertia completion, and the results above. All numbers printed by committed scripts at https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula
notes: ADDENDUM, not a standalone claim. Its purpose is threefold: (i) reduce the published coefficient to a single RATIONAL, a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda) with kappa = 1/2, which sharpens the One Free Number thesis and relocates the transcendence obstruction to general relativity's 8pi rather than to this framework; (ii) ATTACK the parent note's self-cancellation argument at its weakest point -- the free-fall theorem covers only geodesic observers, so a static (non-geodesic) observer at r_cross is a genuine gap -- and report that the null survives quantitatively, worst case 8.85e-14 against a pre-declared 1e-6 threshold; (iii) correct a presentational risk in the parent note AGAINST INTEREST, namely that its (correct) rejection of the 'g >> a0' objection concerns the formal dual and can be misread as claiming a real strong-field signal, when at the framework's operative cosmic scale the effect vanishes by ~22 orders. Strict both-ways discipline: thresholds declared before evaluation, both a0 footings carried, the Nariai coincidence reported with its ~2%-by-chance prior, and Z / kappa / the sign / a0's value all still labelled POSTULATED.
